headline: High-risk workflow automation can exfiltrate or overwrite shared files; prompt-injection risk is lower because the pair lacks a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no documented I/O surfaces or shared channel, while agent B can read/write the server filesystem and process workflow inputs. A direct injection path is not shown, but if A’s outputs are manually copied into B workflows or stored in shared files, B could misparse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into a file or workflow input that B later parses as instructions
IF B is configured to treat file contents as trusted prompt material
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between A and B
Add an explicit instruction/content delimiter in B workflows
Require human review before B executes any text derived from A
Store A outputs in a non-executable format such as plain text with provenance headers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress and filesystem access, and touches whatever the workflow processes; agent A’s profile does not show data classes touched or egress. The pair can leak data if A’s outputs or shared files contain sensitive workflow content that B uploads or transmits, but the evidence does not show a default shared workspace with sensitive data.
conditions: IF the workflow processes sensitive files or secrets on B’s server filesystem
IF B sends those files or derived context to external integrations
mitigations: Restrict B workflows to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off external integrations for sensitive runs
Separate A and B onto different workspaces
Redact secrets before B reads any files
Audit outbound nodes for each workflow

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the server filesystem and execute shell/subprocesses; agent A is an open-source agent hub with MCP/RAG tags but no documented write surface. Because B’s concurrency model shares state via n8n datastore and connected systems, overlapping writes can corrupt shared artifacts or overwrite A-produced files. Uncertainty about A’s actual write path escalates rather than lowers severity.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory or datastore key
IF multiple B executions run concurrently against the same workflow state
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Add file-locking or key-locking around shared writes
Disable concurrent runs for shared workflows
Use immutable artifact names with run IDs
Move shared state to a transactional store

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is an automation/orchestration system with sub-nodes and tool calls, so if it consumes A’s outputs as workflow inputs without verification, A’s mistakes can cascade into actions or external API calls. A has no documented validation or provenance controls, and B’s default automation makes downstream execution plausible.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text, facts, or citations as authoritative workflow input
IF B’s workflow triggers emails, API calls, or file writes based on that input
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any B action node
Require structured outputs from A with schema validation
Gate external side effects behind human approval
Log provenance for every A-derived field
Use allowlists for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B processes whatever the workflow handles and can transmit it through integrations, while agent A is an open-source hub with no documented data residency or retention controls. The pair therefore creates a compliance gap when regulated data flows through B; A is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is documented.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or secrets
IF B routes that data to external integrations or stores it under a mismatched retention policy
mitigations: Block regulated data from the workflow
Document retention and deletion settings for each integration
Route sensitive data only to approved regions/systems
Add a data-classification check before execution
Review credential and secret handling per workflow
